summary: Go SDK graceful-resume loses confirmation header on reconnect leading to duplicate tool execution
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated external webhook side effects (duplicate downstream jobs) after a transient network partition during streaming function calls using Redwood Go SDK. Impact: Duplicate billingable downstream tasks and data duplication in customer systems (patient intake jobs). Environment: Nimbus Health production, running in us-east-1 on Redwood Dedicated pool behind an internal edge-proxy.

Observed behavior: when a long-running orchestration stream reconnects after a short network interruption, the Go SDK resume logic appears to drop or rewrite the function-confirmation header token that the server uses to mark a tool invocation as already-acknowledged. The runtime re-processes the tool call and emits the webhook again, causing duplicate side effects.

Expected behavior: the SDK should preserve confirmation/ack metadata across reconnects or the server should safely deduplicate repeated invocations for the same logical call.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a long-lived streaming session using the Go SDK and issue a function/tool call that triggers an outbound webhook to the customer's downstream job queue.
2) During the inflight function call, simulate a network partition for ~8-20 seconds (TCP connection drop) and allow the SDK to auto-reconnect.
3) Observe server logs and downstream webhook delivery.
4) Repeat several times or under load to reproduce flakiness.

Notes: Customer used default SDK backoff; their orchestration issues a single tool call (no retries from client).
expected_behavior: Single webhook delivery per logical tool invocation even when the SDK reconnects, or clear idempotency/ack confirmation preventing re-execution.
actual_behavior: Duplicate webhook deliveries observed within 30s window after reconnect. The server logged a fresh tool-invocation entry instead of treating it as resumed/inflight. No explicit client retries were observed in the customer's code.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:05:03Z INFO serving-runtime: received tool invocation id=cli-7f4a, confirmation_token=tok-3a9b
2026-03-10T14:05:11Z WARN edge-proxy: connection lost from client_session=cs-91a
2026-03-10T14:05:30Z INFO go-sdk: resumed stream but confirmation_token missing for in-flight call id=cli-7f4a
2026-03-10T14:05:30Z INFO serving-runtime: started new tool invocation id=server-8b2c (correlated_cli_id=cli-7f4a)
2026-03-10T14:05:30Z INFO webhook-delivery: delivered webhook id=wh-002 to https://hooks.nimbus.example/jobs (200)
comments: Amelia Park (support): Customer reports two identical downstream jobs created after a single function call; they see identical payloads with different webhook ids.
Nimbus Health (customer): We did not explicitly retry. This happens intermittently when our edge network blips. This doubled patient intake tasks and requires manual dedupe on our side.

Diego Ramirez (oncall): Assigned for investigation. Initial hypothesis: confirmation/ack header not persisted across reconnect in Go SDK; server treats resumed connection as new invocation if header absent.

SRE (investigation): Observed correlation id present in telemetry but confirmation_token field empty in resumed stream frames. Edge-proxy logs show a rewrite of some headers during connection migration.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in a staging replica with connection drop at 10s: resumed client frames contained correlation_id but confirmation_token was zero-length.
- Edge proxy (sidecar) has a known behavior of trimming custom binary metadata on h2 connection migration in our current config version (v2.3.1).
- Go SDK uses an in-memory ephemeral buffer for confirmation tokens attached to the stream; on reconnect the SDK replays frames but due to a race between resume ACK injection and backpressure flush, the token can be omitted.
- Serving runtime does not currently dedupe solely on (client_id + payload hash) for streaming funcalls because some customers rely on server-side re-execution semantics.

Hypothesis: combination of edge-proxy header canonicalization and SDK resume race leads to the confirmation token being missing on the resumed frame, which the runtime interprets as a fresh invocation.
root_cause: Loss of the per-invocation confirmation_token during stream reconnection caused by (1) edge-proxy stripping/rewriting custom metadata on connection migration and (2) Go SDK race where confirmation metadata is not persisted to the reconnect buffer before frame replay.
mitigation:
Short-term: recommend customer enable a conservative client-side retry-suppress header and add webhook-level dedup keys on their consumer (downstream) to filter duplicates. We pushed a temporary edge-proxy config that preserves custom metadata for stream resumes in us-east-1 pool.

Long-term: coordinated fix planned across SDK and serving runtime: persist confirmation token across reconnects in the Go SDK and add server-side dedupe based on (invocation-id || canonical payload hash || idempotency header).
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: updated edge-proxy config to stop trimming custom stream metadata (rolled to affected nodes in the customer's Dedicated pool). Customer applied webhook dedupe on their queue and confirmed duplicates stopped after roll.
Engineering actions: patch for Go SDK to atomically persist and replay confirmation metadata in a reconnect-safe buffer has landed in PR 4127. Server dedupe task created and scheduled for next sprint.
related_workarounds_provided: 1) Enabled edge-proxy preserve-metadata flag for customer's dedicated pool. 2) Provided example snippet for customers to set X-Redwood-Idempotency header at call-site. 3) Recommended downstream webhook idempotency keys (X-Dedupe-Key) and retention window.
follow_up_tasks: PR: go-sdk patch to persist confirmation metadata across reconnects - review and merge (assigned Diego)
Server: implement payload-hash dedupe for streaming funcalls - create design doc and schedule (owner: Runtime team)
Docs: update streaming idempotency guidance and add a troubleshooting section for reconnection duplicates
Tests: add chaos test to CI that simulates connection migration and validates no duplicate tool-side effects
